section_summary: This section contains monthly political reports and diplomatic correspondence from the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo covering April, May, and June 1940. It documents mounting strains in Japanese-American relations, Japanese policy towards the European conflict and the status of the Netherlands East Indies, negotiations with Great Britain over Tientsin, and military operations in China. The records also detail Embassy representations over detained personnel (Satoru Sugimura and C. Matsuo), domestic Japanese economic pressures such as rice shortages and price control, and the exploratory Grew-Arita conversations.

subfiles.about: Concluding part of Embassy Tokyo's monthly report on political and economic conditions in Japan for April 1940, with comprehensive schedules of telegrams and despatches sent to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Reviews the draft formula negotiated with Great Britain regarding Chinese silver and police arrangements in the British Concession at Tientsin, as well as an understanding permitting Norwegian merchant vessels to trade with Japanese ports. Surveys military operations in southeastern Shansi along the Yellow River, General Abe's diplomatic mission to the Wang Ching-wei regime in Nanking, and official declarations insisting upon the political and economic status quo of the Netherlands East Indies following German moves in Europe. Outlines internal Japanese developments including Foreign Office expansion, army six-year armaments replenishment, price control commissions, bond absorption issues, and wartime economic regulations. Concludes with complete chronological registers of telegrams and despatches transmitted to the State Department during April 1940.
subfiles.title: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of April 1940 (Report No. 163)

subfiles.about: Embassy Tokyo Despatch No. 4885 transmitting Report No. 164 on political, economic, diplomatic, and military conditions in Japan during May 1940, with correspondence schedules.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Documents discussions between Foreign Minister Hachiro Arita and visiting U.S. High Commissioner to the Philippines Francis B. Sayre regarding Philippine immigration quotas, alongside diplomatic friction over the military arrest of consular interpreter C. Matsuo in Taihoku and Embassy translator Satoru Sugimura in Tokyo. Details Japanese anxieties over the Netherlands East Indies following the German invasion of the Low Countries, Anglo-Japanese negotiations over Tientsin, French protests regarding air attacks on the Yunnan Railway, and anti-Japanese riots in Lima. Analyzes the creation of an inner Cabinet four-minister conference, acute domestic rice shortages leading to hoarding and planned Kwansai rationing, skilled labor shortages, and suppression of labor parties. Appends complete logs of telegrams and despatches forwarded to the Department of State throughout May 1940.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4885: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of May 1940 (Report No. 164)

subfiles.about: Embassy Tokyo Despatch No. 4958 transmitting Report No. 165 on political and economic conditions in Japan during June 1940, covering the exploratory Grew-Arita conversations.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Presents Ambassador Grew's assessment of political factionalism in Japan and the strengthening of pro-German elements following Axis victories in Western Europe. Reports on a sequence of confidential, informal conversations between Ambassador Grew and Foreign Minister Hachiro Arita exploring potential paths toward stabilizing American-Japanese relations and settling the China conflict without sacrificing core principles. Summarizes Japanese proposals for a commercial modus vivendi and the cessation of Western assistance to Chiang Kai-shek, breaking off mid-discussion during Foreign Minister Arita's oral statement of June 28 regarding immigration and trade controls.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4958: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of June 1940 (Report No. 165)
